subject: Evaluation success heuristics, exit gates & acceptance test plan (HelioHealth)
messages:
From: Hannah Li <hannah.li@heliohealth.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@heliohealth.com>
Date: 2025-09-10T14:23:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff notes — acceptance guardrails we discussed

Rafael — thanks again for Tuesday's demo. Team wants a concise acceptance plan we can use for our internal stakeholders (Clinical Ops, IT, Procurement). High level asks:

- Narrow list of success metrics (latency, FPR for routing, throughput) with pass thresholds
- Concrete exit gates for the 4-week evaluation (what makes this a "go")
- A set of reproducible acceptance tests we can run with our sample data

Can you share a single-sheet with responsibilities and timelines so I can run it by Procurement? Daniel — looping you in for procurement constraints (data retention, audit logs).

Thanks,
Hannah
Director, Clinical Data Innovation
HelioHealth
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Li <hannah.li@heliohealth.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@heliohealth.com>
Date: 2025-09-11T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff notes — acceptance guardrails we discussed

Hannah — appreciate the clear ask. Attached is a first-pass MAP & acceptance plan (HL_MAP_v1.2.xlsx) and a short smoke-test script doc. Key highlights in-line below for quick review; more detail in the sheet.

High-level success metrics (pass if ALL satisfied):
- Median inference latency (p50) <= 250ms for 95% of test queries under your demo workload
- End-to-end throughput >= 6k tokens/sec sustained across 10-minute windows
- Semantic match F1 >= 0.86 on the clinical QA test set (sample included)
- No data leakage: KV cache isolation validated via sample tenant vectors

Exit gates (week-by-week):
- Week 1: Environment and data ingestion validated; smoke scripts pass (low bar)
- Week 2: Latency and KV isolation tests pass with synthetic load
- Week 3: Concordance and clinical QA tests executed; F1 >= 0.86 required
- Week 4: Ops checklist and SLA report; sign-off or rollback decision

Responsibility matrix (short):
- Redwood (Rafael, Ben): infra, test harness, SLA report, remediation runbook
- Helio (Hannah, Daniel): supply sample data/labels, run local compliance checks, procurement signoff
- Lauren: escalation owner / exec contact if performance breaches during testing

Attachments: HL_MAP_v1.2.xlsx (MAP, timeline, owners), redwood-eval-smoke-scripts.md (step-by-step), redwood-sla-summary.pdf

Would you like this converted to a single one-pager (PDF) for Procurement? If so, we can deliver by end of day Friday, 9/12.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

--
Attachment stubs:
- HL_MAP_v1.2.xlsx (spreadsheet)
- redwood-eval-smoke-scripts.md (text)
- redwood-sla-summary.pdf (pdf)
From: Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@heliohealth.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>, Hannah Li <hannah.li@heliohealth.com>
Date: 2025-09-12T10:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff notes — acceptance guardrails we discussed

Thanks — that looks good. Two Procurement items:
1) We need a clear data-retention window and audit-log sample (are retention controls configurable per-tenant?).
2) If the Week 3 concordance test fails by more than 5% relative to the threshold, Procurement requires a written remediation plan and an extension option (one week) before we move to production.

Can Redwood confirm retention settings and provide an example audit log extract (redacted) for review?

—Daniel
Head of Procurement, HelioHealth
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@heliohealth.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>, Hannah Li <hannah.li@heliohealth.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-09-13T11:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff notes — acceptance guardrails we discussed

Daniel — quick answers below and attached a redacted audit log sample (in the XLSX).

- Retention: tenant-level retention windows are configurable; we can set a 30-day default for the pilot and demonstrate via config snapshot. Full HSM/KMS integration available for Private deployments (per your compliance note).
- Audit logs: we will provide a redacted extract showing request id, timestamp, model version, and action (read/write/cache-evict).
- Remediation/extension: agreed — if Week 3 misses the concordance threshold by >5% we'll produce a root-cause analysis and offer a one-week remediation window with a clear rollback plan.

Next step: Rafael and I will run the smoke scripts on Monday against your sample bundle. Rafael — can we lock Monday 9/15 10:00am PT for the baseline run?

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Senior Customer Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Li <hannah.li@heliohealth.com>, Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@heliohealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-09-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff notes — acceptance guardrails we discussed

Quick status update after the baseline run this morning (results attached in the MAP sheet):

- Environment: OK — data ingested, KV isolation confirmed for tenant scope
- Latency: p50 = 235ms, p95 = 480ms under demo traffic (meets threshold)
- Throughput: peaked at 6.2k tokens/sec sustained under 10-minute windows
- Clinical QA: initial concordance F1 = 0.863 (just above 0.86 threshold)

Given the numbers we recommend moving to Week 2 plan (load soak + extended KV tests). The MAP spreadsheet now includes a week-by-week checklist and sign-off cells for each stakeholder.

Action items for Helio: please confirm Procurement's acceptance of the one-week remediation clause and sign the MAP sheet in Drive (link below) so we can schedule the full soak next Tuesday.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/open?id=hl-map-2025

If there are no objections, we'll update the HubSpot deal with the Week 1 report and the next milestone (Week 2 soak scheduled 9/23).

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
